newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Four groups shortlisted for Manila water scheme.
newsitem.headline: Four groups shortlisted for Manila water scheme.

text.p: Manila's Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS) has come up with a short list of four groups for its privatisation, the International Finance Corp (IFC) said on Wednesday.

IFC's corporate finance services manager Scott McLeod told a news conference the four groups, each made up of a local company and a foreign partner, had submitted a second batch of submissions last Friday.

McLeod identified them as Aboitiz Equity Ventures Inc with Compagnie Generale des Eaux of France; Ayala Land Inc with a joint venture firm of Bechtel Enterprises and Northwest Water of Britain; Benpres Holdings Corp with Lyonnaise des Eaux SA, and Metro Pacific Corp and Anglian Water Plc.
"These submissions have been received and are now being reviewed for final prequalification," he said.
IFC, the private sector financing arm of the World Bank, is advising MWSS on the privatisation process.

McLeod said three other Filipino companies which had earlier qualified to take part in the bidding but which had not been able to get an international partner, were still welcome to be partners in one of these four groups.
The companies are House of Investments, JG Summit Holdings Inc and Filinvest Land Inc.
Under the privatisation rules, the competing consortia should be 60 percent owned by Filipinos.
The bidding for two 25-year service contracts for the country's largest water utility has been scheduled for the end of the year, with the final contract to be awarded in January.
